BEERCRUSH is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome BEERCRUSH soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome An highly addictive arcade runner with an art style I personally find charming, akin to pizza tower Some pros: -The slight variations to the maps and songs in different runs really sold me on the depth and helped different runs to feel unique -The controls are super intuitive and unique in my opinion; only using mouse movement + left and right controls feels surprisingly good and makes this game feel like a tight package. I have found that having the camera move behind with the minigames is a good example of the controls aiding the gameplay as this can add a layer of depth that keeps the minigames feeling fresh over time as you have to make sure you face the correct orientation when resuming your run. this game is simple, but BEERCRUSH gets so much out of its mechanics. The quick drop from mid air is also so satisfying and something I could not live without. My only very slight nit-picks which are more preference than critique is that I wish there were more / caps were slightly more varied in abilities as I tend to end up using the same build every playthrough and that I wish your hitbox at end of the slide animation was slightly more forgiving as I've had multiple times where I've gotten up slightly too early and bashed my big skull on something that looks paper thin (although I'm sure this is a skill issue and ill get used to it over time) Overall, I give BEERCRUSH 10 drunken beers, very much worth the money

If the world is against BEERCRUSH, I'm against the world. If BEERCRUSH has no fans, I'm dead. On a serious note, this is genuinely one of the greatest runner games I have ever played. Simple controls that feel natural while also allowing for fast paced, fluid movement. Worlds that are challenging yet balanced [spoiler](yes, even city to an extent)[/spoiler] in addition to being unique from one another and having pretty cool alternate variants. The drinking minigames are fun to engage in and fit the world they're located in while also allowing you to redirect yourself once regular gameplay resumes, making the different gameplay styles work together surprising well. The roguelike elements help to bring much needed variety while not being intrusive on the core runner gameplay. In case that wasn't enough, there are 6 game modes, including a faster, runner gameplay only mode, a WarioWare-like mode and an endless mode that quickly ramps up in difficulty. The game also has mod support through the Steam Workshop. The game's presentation hits hard, with the graphics being simple yet charming and easy on the eyes. The shaders, camera effects, particles and sound effects all make the game feel super responsive and alive. The soundtrack? HOLY CRAP! Absolute ear heaven! It rivals the video game OST greats like Pizza Tower and Sonic Mania. The game even has some lore to it, with John Beer (the player character) being a divorced alcoholic who tries to stop his alcohol addiction from further ruining his life. To top it off, the game features optional voice acting for the shop intermissions between worlds. It reminds me of the Chaos Wars English dub in the best possible way, as the crude VA work actually fits the crude style of the game and was likely done by one of the 2 developers on this game. Yes, the game was created by only 2 developers, with both of them being students who created this game for a university game jam. Pretty cool, right? However, I do have some minor issues, such as the pool of bottlecaps being quite small [spoiler](only 19 caps, of which 16 are accessible through standard means)[/spoiler], the difficulty occasionally spiking at certain worlds and the act of falling into the void being an instant death, which can be quite off putting for first time players, though it does make sense as it prevents the worlds that feature the void from being easily cheesed. To conclude, this is a phenomenal game that everyone must try at least once, especially when its full price is only a little over 4 quid. It's one of the very few games where I would recommend paying full price instead of waiting around for a sale. To dragonsploder and pretzol, thank you for creating BEERCRUSH, it's seriously one of the most fun games I have ever played, even during the moments where I rage. I hope this game becomes popular one day and I wish you two the best for any future projects. To everyone else, TLDR: BEERCRUSH is a healthy alternative to actually drinking beer and you should play it.

This game is seriously addictive. The gameplay is very fun and the soundtrack really makes it hype! All the different game modes and even the different endings to the game bring so much to it that I really appreciate. I was surprised by how much I enjoy the short story within the game. I'm a sucker for story, and yet its simplicity and feel-good nature of the ending (especially on Wasted) was something I loved. Even the short times you get to see the only other NPC: Kyle, in the shop are enjoyable. I just like his dialogue and how he changes his sprite for the Freezer and Freezer Alt as well. The ONLY thing I would ask that they add into the game is a quick restart button. I know it's not very necessary for the main game modes, but when attempting the challenges such as Big Beer's Brew, it would be nice to have. All in all, there's a surprising amount of content and every bit of it is very enjoyable!
